title: Do you actually build your games with AI, or do you use it as another tool in your development workflow?
author: benmar0834
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/gdnfs99hbn3i1.png

https://i.redd.it/65g7x99hbn3i1.png

I've been wondering how other indie developers here are actually using generative AI.

Are you building entire games through prompting, including code, mechanics and assets? Do you already have a programming background and use AI to speed things up, or have you managed to create a functioning game with little to no coding experience?

I'm asking because my own experience has been pretty interesting.

I'm developing a 2D visual novel called **Succubus Island**, and AI has been a huge part of making this project possible.

I'm mainly a Python developer, but I'm far from an experienced programmer. I've used AI extensively as a coding assistant, and some of the things I've managed to implement would have been extremely difficult for me to tackle alone.

A few examples:

* **Minigame integration:** I've integrated completely separate minigames into my visual novel, including their logic, interactions and connection to the main game.
* **UI and systems:** I've used AI to troubleshoot bugs, improve interfaces and implement gameplay features.
* **Localization:** More recently, I used AI to help translate a substantial part of the game into Spanish. The results have been surprisingly good, although there's still room for human proofreading.

One thing worth mentioning is that I don't generate all my artwork with AI. Most of the final character artwork and illustrations are commissioned from artists. In my case, AI has been much more valuable as a development assistant than as an art generator.

I'm not going to pretend AI did everything for me. I still have to understand what I'm implementing, test it, fix things when they break and make the actual design decisions. But it definitely allowed me to take on features that would otherwise have been outside my reach.

**I'm curious about your experiences:**

1. How much of your game is actually made with AI?
2. Do you have programming experience, or did you learn along the way with AI?
3. Has anyone here managed to build an entire game almost exclusively through prompting?

I'd genuinely like to compare workflows and hear what has worked (and what has been a complete disaster) for other developers.

If anyone is curious about the project itself, here's the project page: [https://succubusisland.itch.io/succubusisland](https://succubusisland.itch.io/succubusisland)

comments.author: Fancy-Proof-9449
comments.body:
Pretty much the whole game through AI here, and I have no programming background. I don't write code at all. I tell Claude what I want, it builds it, and I judge it by playing on my phone. It's a mobile arcade game that's live on Google Play now.

What made that possible wasn't clever prompting. It was two things. A rules file in the project that says what must never break and why, which the AI reads every session. And automated checks that run on every build, so when the AI breaks something it didn't mean to, the build fails instead of me finding out on my phone a day later.

The disaster story: early on I had the AI save and commit after every single reply. It committed half-finished work in the middle of a change and broke another project of mine. Now it only commits when something is finished and the checks pass.

Like you, the design calls are still mine. The AI is great at building what I describe and pretty bad at knowing whether it's fun.
